I played as the Dominican Republic last season from 2027 until 2040 and here I'll walk you through a summary of some of what I did, some of what I wanted to do, and some of what I shouldn't have done. If you want to look into everything I did, check out this wiki. I am not going through all the technical information to claiming and playing but this might give you some idea of what the game is like and how you might consider playing it. Consider this:

 

PNTBTR'S GUIDE TO MODERNPOWERS

 

Intro

 

I, like so many others, stumbled into ModernPowers on accident and quickly saw the fun that could be had in such an open, sandbox-style game. One of the most important things to note is that there is no single way to play the game. You can play it more or less as you see fit, the only real rules are keeping realism up, neither flooding nor abandoning the subverse, and appropriately tagging posts for the mods.

 

Claiming

 

First off, choosing a country. It is, of course, helpful to choose a country you already know something about but I went the opposite direction and chose a country I knew almost nothing about. On the plus side, this made researching topics to post on more interesting to me, but there was also the negative side that because I had no prior experience with the country and because the Dominican Republic is a pretty small, out of the way country, I spent an inordinate amount of time researching miserably boring subjects to ensure the airtight levels of realism I was playing with (which are not expected of every player).

Next you will want to choose some general long term goals to strive for, be they military, diplomatic, economic, social, or whatever. My main goal was to unify the island of Hispaniola through invasion/annexation of Haiti. The mods responded that this would likely take decades and they weren't kidding. In 13 years of play, I made very modest progress in being able to plausibly invade Haiti as I had to set up not only the right military conditions to take and hold the land but create a diplomatic environment in which an invasion wouldn't cause the US or UN to step in. I did, however, make great strides in shorter term socio-economic goals such as education improvement.

 

The Early Years

 

Most players, myself included, jump the gun and call themselves president or choose a president off the bat but for realism's sake, you can't really do that. I ended up playing off my Presidente Peanut as actual Dominican Republic President Danilo Medina having a stroke which later caused him to retire.

I felt the first step to invading Haiti would be to put together a modern fleet of helicopters. Not one to be direct, I decided to ask the US for some ancient Vietnam War era helicopters from the US, which then predictably ran into troubles, forcing the President to address the situation and later begin research on a new helicopter with a friendly nation with an aeronautical industry. Note: you can't pull researchers out of your ass. You can develop university departments, partner with other nations, trade, steal, or think of other ways to get what you want.

I then proceeded to create what is probably the most confusing way possible to elect a new president, announcing candidates, observing the campaign, and, finally, rolling for and announcing the winner of the election. While my method created what I would consider a more realistic election, it also meant every 4 weeks I had to go back and figure out how to run my election and then explain to the mods how it worked.

I decided to leave my short term goals to the President of the time, effectively making my gameplay depend almost completely on rolls. I was fine with this but it may not be what you are looking for. If you are a major country, internal politics should play at least some role in your game. though.

This President promised a new education system so, after ungodly amounts of research, I put together a wholly new national education system to be implemented over originally 10 and later 15 years. Putting this together involved a good amount of set up as well as I gave the existing education infrastructure to the Catholic Diocese,, made a public appeal for more foreign teachers, and expanded the scope of my main university.

 

Some More Years

 

After getting my feet under me, I decided to pursue some more aggressive policies. Most notably, a request for illegal Haitian immigrants to leave. Followed by forced deportations of the immigrants, which resulted in a number of mistakes and tragedies for the nation culminating in a diplomatic solution with a neighbor, an amnesty for the immigrants still in the country, and even a faked suicide attempt by the President in order to garner sympathy.

I also put together a new bullet train line and high speed train network which was as much a way to transport tourists around the country and students to the central education center in the capital, Santo Domingo, as it was a way to deliver troops to the Haitian border.

The Dominican Republic was elected to fill one of the temporary UN Security Council seats. I used this opportunity to press hard for harsh sanctions against another country that invaded its neighbor, with full knowledge that these attempts would fail and the precedent set to do nothing when a country invades its neighbor for "humane" reasons.

 

The Communist Years

 

In a big surprise, a Communist leader was elected President and I had to quickly come up with a reason why they would win. This change in politics brought reinvigorated economic plans such as an expansion to existing mining operations and the Caribbean's first ski hill.

Part of the new Communist plan included replacing the country's coast guard and selling the newly completed Dominican-British helicopter as well as a general expansion to the military and its bases.

 

The Lost Future

 

Unfortunately, at this point, the game was such a huge time sink and I had other things going on so I stopped there but I still had a number of ideas to implement including:

-An A to Z restructuring of the country's budget which I had previously been just patching on top of previous budgets (budget management, by the way, is ludicrous micromanagement nobody expects you to do - just bear in mind what kind of costs your country can afford).

-Upgrading the country's water treatment capabilities, giving potable water to almost every citizen.

-Creating a civil defense force/militia (which may later turn into a rebel group)

-Preparing infrastructure for the rapid invasion of Haiti

 

The Rapid Invasion of Haiti

 

My plan for invading Haiti called for a two-pronged north/south land invasion that would be preceded by a massive helicopter movement to immediately seize the UN headquarters, and the couple of airports and seaports that the country has. This would have been carried out only after the US/UN's focus was elsewhere (most likely our new ally China) for diminished response capabilities and willpower as well as provide maximum havoc on the world. I was also hoping to spark a new Cuban Missile Crisis by hosting Chinese nukes.
